_README: What actually happened, annotated BY A HUMAN, LIVE, while the trace was recording.
Without this file 'no flapping' is unfalsifiable: a filter that reports nobody was ever
here also never flaps (#225 AC-4), so the replay asserts both halves — agreement with
these transitions AND a bound on the total decision count.
Times are SECONDS FROM THE START OF THE TRACE, matching the `t` field of its rows.
They were logged by keypress as each event happened and converted from absolute UTC
against the trace's own `_meta.recorded_utc`. They were NOT read back off the trace:
that would be circular, since the trace is precisely what these are here to falsify.
`slack` is how many decisions beyond `len(arrivals) + len(departures)` the replay
tolerates. Raising it to make a run pass defeats the test — the bound IS the criterion
(#225 AC-7). Tune the filter windows against the trace instead, and record before/after.

_note: Recorded 2026-08-15 13:45:13Z on the bring-up rig: ov5647 at 640x480, detector_scale 1,
3 fps, confidence_threshold 0.35, gain 1.2 s, lose 75 s. 10800 frames, 60.2 min, 0 error
frames. Ordinary desk work — reading, typing, turning to a second screen — with four real
trips out of the room lasting between 4 and 8 minutes.
A FIFTH arrival was marked at t=3623.6, 13.5 s AFTER the recorder stopped at t=3610.1.
It is deliberately absent: an annotation outside the recorded window is not evidence
about this trace, and including it would assert a decision the frames cannot contain.
Between t=1075 and t=1195 — inside the first away window — the detector produced a burst
of false positives on something in the upper-right of the empty room (81% across, 20%
down, avg confidence 0.42 against 0.68 for the real person, who sits at 57%/60%). They
are NOT annotated because nobody was there. The filter correctly ignores them at every
threshold from 0.35 to 0.60: they are scattered rather than sustained, so they never fill
the gain window. That is the hysteresis doing its job, and it is why this trace is worth
keeping even though it contains detector noise.
